Previously: `strftime` gives us the hour of each watch reading — but as text, like `'18'`.
To compare it as a number we change its **type**.
`CAST(value AS data_type)` changes a value's type. `CAST(strftime('%H', ts) AS INTEGER)` turns `'18'` into the number 18.

beats.ask: All the details of logs from hour **18 onwards**, comparing the hour as a **number**.

hints.skeleton: SELECT * FROM watch_log WHERE CAST(strftime('%H', ts) AS ____) >= 18;

traps.reply: Every row came back — even 6 AM! `strftime` gives **text** ('06'), and SQLite treats text as bigger than any number. `CAST` it to INTEGER first.
